title: KVCache momentum eviction surge & ghost-entry sanitization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a capacity spike on 2026-03-07 we observed a transient but repeatable surge of eviction churn in the KV cache which generated a class of "ghost" entries: small metadata-only entries that survived eviction and led to elevated memory accounting and degraded tail latencies for tenant workloads. The issue manifested as increased request latencies (95th/99th) and elevated OOM pressure in a handful of Dedicated pools for ~45m.

Why this ticket exists:
This ticket captures the follow-up plan and action items after the immediate mitigation. It consolidates findings (root cause hypotheses, probes, and telemetry gaps), defines short-term hardening, and schedules longer-term runtime fixes and e2e tests to prevent recurrence.

Incident timeline (abridged):
- 2026-03-07 02:14 UTC — Pager triggered for Dedicated pool us-west-2-g-12, 95th latency spike observed. Alerts: high eviction rate, memory growth.
- 2026-03-07 02:20 UTC — Oncall invoked emergency mem-throttle; autoscaler temporarily limited allocations.
- 2026-03-07 02:37 UTC — Engineering activated temporary eviction-smoothing flag (hotfix) and flushed stale prefix indexes; latencies recovered by 02:59.
- 2026-03-07 03:15 UTC — Incident declared mitigated; postmortem investigation started.

Root cause (current understanding):
- An eviction-score "momentum" update (introduced in runtime-1.18 to bias recently-used items) interacts poorly with async compact/rehash race windows. Under high churn (bursty traffic pattern) the score decay code incremented a per-entry momentum counter in a non-atomic path, exposing a reorder where an entry would be marked for eviction but reinserted with stale metadata. This produced tiny "ghost" entries: malformed index references with no valid value pointer but a live metadata header that escaped normal TTL sweeps.
- The ghost entries are counted by the slab allocator and by the memory accounting path, but because they lack a backing payload they confuse eviction heuristics and artificially increase perceived occupancy, triggering an eviction storm and thrashing.
- Telemetry gaps: we had no high-cardinality series for momentum counter deltas, and no histogram of "index-entry size vs payload size" to surface metadata-only entries. This slowed root cause discovery.

Immediate mitigations taken during incident:
- Flipped eviction-smoothing flag to conservative mode (hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/11987).
- Manually ran a prefix-index sanitization sweep on affected shards to remove ghost entries (runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/kvcache-runbooks#sanitization).
- Temporarily reduced per-tenant cache quotas for busiest tenants for 2 hours to limit churn.

Short-term action items (0–2 weeks):
- AI1 — Add atomic guard on momentum updates in the fast path to prevent reorder races — Owner: Marco Ruiz — Estimate: 2 — Status: In Progress
- AI2 — Implement a periodic ghost-entry detector that computes (index_entry_size - payload_size) histogram and emits alert when metadata-only entries > threshold — Owner: Priya Shenoy — Estimate: 3 — Status: Planned
- AI3 — Extend existing eviction telemetry to include momentum-counter deltas as a per-shard histogram (1m/5m) and tenant-scoped cardinality — Owner: Devin Park — Estimate: 3 — Status: Planned
- AI4 — Backfill retroactive run of sanitization sweep to all Dedicated pools and add an automated weekly sweep job — Owner: SRE Team (oncall rotation) — Estimate: 2 — Status: In Progress
- AI5 — Add e2e load test that reproduces bursty insert/evict patterns to catch momentum-eviction interactions in CI -> runtime stress stage — Owner: QA (Load) — Estimate: 5 — Status: Planned

Longer-term fixes (2–8 weeks):
- LF1 — Revisit eviction scoring design: remove per-entry mutable momentum in hot path; move to lightweight sampling-based bias or decay-on-access performed under lockless epoch — Owner: Runtime Architecture — Estimate: 8 — Status: Proposed
- LF2 — Rework slab allocator accounting to differentiate metadata-only headers so eviction heuristics can treat them as low-value for eviction order and avoid overcounting — Owner: Memory Team — Estimate: 6 — Status: Proposed

Acceptance criteria / Definition of done for short-term items:
- Momentum atomic guard merged and deployed in runtime-1.19 canary with no regression on tail-latency for standard workloads.
- Ghost-entry detector produces signal in staging with synthetic workload and a noisy alert threshold; alert routed to kvcache-pager.
- Weekly sanitization job created with automated rollback safe-mode.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Canary rollout in us-west-2 small cluster for 72h with momentum guard only. Monitor 95th/99th latency, eviction rate, and ghost-entry histogram.
- If green, progressive rollout to Dedicated pools with 10% increments over 24h windows until 100%.

Post-incident artifacts and links:
- Postmortem notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/kvcache/postmortems/momentum-eviction-2026-03-07
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/11987
- Sanitization sweep job: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/d/ops/kvcache-sweeps?orgId=1
- Alert: https://monitoring.redwood.ai/alerts/EVICT_CHURN_USW2

Risks and open questions:
- Will atomicizing momentum updates add measurable latency in the hot write path? (benchmarks planned in AI1).
- Potential for similar races in other mutable per-entry fields (e.g., prefetch score) — we need a sweep for all mutable metadata fields.
- Need to quantify how often ghost entries have been created historically — will require a one-time cluster-wide scan (data-retention considerations).
